To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the concomitant treatment of a diabetes-resistant rat with an islet xenograt and the immunosuppressive drug cyclosporin results in the long-term acceptance and maintenance of normoglycaemia in the recipient, while the same combination of xenograt and drug is ineffective in the diabetes-prone rat.
islet xenografted into the abdominal testis of diabetes-resistant ACI rats survived for >4 months, but only if the rats were treated with CsA.
the concomitant use of CsA with an antigenic islets xenograft led to an extended duration of normoglycermia in diabetes-resistant but only transient normoglycermic in diabetes-prone recipients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an immunologically privileged site for islet xenografted in the abdominal testis of rats.
the survival and function of islet xenotransplants.
the development of an islet xenogeneic transplantation model in rats.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CsA therapy is capable of prolonging the survival of islets transplanted into the abdominal testis in diabetes-resistant but apparently not in diabetes-proneness rats.
the testicular microenvironment is not a suitable site for islet xenografted survival in BB/Wor rats.
islets xenografted into the abdominal testis of normal, diabetes-prone rats can be protected from immunological attack for prolonged periods by the concomitant use of CsA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the testicular microenvironment provides a favorable milieu for xenograft survival, but the host's immune status may be a critical factor.
the testis may be the best site for islet xenogratfs in the diabetic rat.
the testes of the BB/W rats are not suitable for xenograft survival.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the BB/Wor rat is a poor candidate for the long-term xenografting of islets.
the BB/Wor rat model of spontaneous autoimmune diabetes is not a good model to study long-term tolerance to islet allografts or xenografts.
the testes are an excellent site for islet xenografted survival, and that CsA therapy can induce long-term normoglycemy in ACI and W/L rats, but not in diabetes prone BB/Wor rats.
